newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey shares up 2.2 pct as holiday delays payments.
newsitem.headline: Turkey shares up 2.2 pct as holiday delays payments.

text.p: Istanbul shares gained an average 2.2 percent on Tuesday in an awaited rise ahead of an approaching holiday which caused settlements of transactions to be delayed to next week, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed 33 points, or 2.2 percent higher at 1,535. Trade volume increased to 17.52 trillion lira ($132.2 million) from Monday's 13.13 trillion ($99.5 million).

A 4-1/2-day religious holiday between April 17-21 will be followed by an official holiday on April 23. The stock market will close from mid-Thursday until April 24 as the government declared April 22 holiday for public offices.
Today's transactions will be settled on April 24 and Wednesday's deals on April 25.

"There was buying because of the opportunity that payments are delayed to after the holiday. But the volume is still low and trade is unsettled because of politics. Particularly, the National Security Council meeting (due on April 26) unnerves the market," said Orhan Ozbuldu from Guven securities.
Investors switching to cash or repo deals ahead of the holiday had caused volume to shrink last week and on Monday.
